description: Sabotages for windows-file-watcher. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: This manifest was created for one guard and is deliberately not a survey of the crate. The servicing path's shutdown ordering is here because its window is a few instructions wide, cannot be reached by timing, and the guard for it was wrong on the first attempt -- which is exactly the shape that needs something re-running it rather than a command somebody ran once. The rest of the crate's teardown is covered by windows-threadpool-sys' manifest, since the obligations it rests on are that crate's.
whyTestArgs: The drain obligation is only enforced with `fail-fast`, and this crate does not expose that feature itself -- it arrives through `windows-threadpool-sys`. Without it a sabotage to a teardown path is reported rather than failed, and the sweep records SURVIVED for a guard that is present and working.

sabotages.name: shutdown stops waiting for a producer that has not published yet
sabotages.why: `submit` releases the queue lock after deciding to ring and only then calls `ThreadpoolWork::submit`, so a producer preempted between the two has committed to publishing and is invisible to anyone holding the lock. Without this wait, `shut_down` can close the queue and run its whole cancellation inside that window, and the publication lands after it has returned -- contradicting its own documented guarantee that no drain can start afterwards. The guard drives the interleaving through a test-only gate rather than hoping to hit it, and asserts the happens-before (a marker the releasing thread sets before it releases) rather than any state the queue carries. That distinction is the reason this entry exists: the first version of the guard asserted only the ring count, the closed flag and the handler count, every one of which is true whether or not the wait is there, and it passed six times out of six with the wait deleted. The current one is caught 8 of 8.

sabotages.name: M17.1: a case-insensitive directory compares case-sensitively
sabotages.why: The case choice is the only thing that makes a file route match a differently cased stored name.

sabotages.name: M17.1: a case-sensitive directory folds case
sabotages.why: On a case-sensitive directory A.txt and a.txt are different files, and folding routes one's changes to the other's subscription.

sabotages.name: M17.1: a comparison that says less is a match
sabotages.why: Only an equal result is the same name.

sabotages.name: M17.1: a name too long for the call is not compared exactly
sabotages.why: Reaching it takes a slice of more than 2^31 units, so it is observed through the comparison's result: the fallback is the exact comparison, and equal names must still match.

sabotages.name: M17.1: a failure of the call is a match
sabotages.why: A failed comparison must never route a change to a subscription.

sabotages.name: M17.1 control: the equal result is read through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same comparison through a local, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: D-87: the shared doorbell is an event of its own
sabotages.why: A shared holder is meant to be one more owner of the queue's event. A handle to a different event is silent: it never signals, and a thread-pool wait armed on it never fires. The raw handle equal to the queue's and the wake tests see it.
find:
self.ensure_doorbell()?;
        Ok(self
            .shared
            .doorbell
            .get()
            .expect("the doorbell was just created")
            .clone())

sabotages.name: D-87: the shared doorbell is taken without creating it
sabotages.why: The first ask for any doorbell creates it. A shared form that skips that finds nothing to clone, which the test that asks for the shared form first sees as a panic.
find:
self.ensure_doorbell()?;
        Ok(self
            .shared
            .doorbell
            .get()
            .expect("the doorbell was just created")
            .clone())

sabotages.name: D-87 control: the shared doorbell is converted into its own type
sabotages.why: A control: `.into()` from the type to itself, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
find:
self.ensure_doorbell()?;
        Ok(self
            .shared
            .doorbell
            .get()
            .expect("the doorbell was just created")
            .clone())
replace:
self.ensure_doorbell()?;
        Ok(self
            .shared
            .doorbell
            .get()
            .expect("the doorbell was just created")
            .clone().into())
